uncited: **Inputs:** An octree data structure (built via Wilhelms and Van Gelder's method) containing min-max values at each node; a viewpoint; an isovalue.
**Outputs:** A stream of triangles forwarded to the graphics accelerator.
**Virtual Screen:** A bitmap with one bit per pixel.
**Hierarchical Tiles:** A coverage map is an 8x8 rectangular bitmap where each bit represents a pixel.
Tiles are organized hierarchically into meta-tiles.
**Front-to-Back Traversal:** Traverse the octree in front-to-back order relative to the viewpoint.
**Coarse Software Visibility Test:** For each meta-cell intersecting the isosurface, perform a visibility test to determine if it is hidden by previously extracted sections.
*   **Pruning Logic:** Project the meta-cell onto the virtual screen.
If any pixel in the projection is unset (visible), the cell is visible.
**Forward Triangulation:** Triangulate visible cells and forward the resulting triangles to the graphics accelerator for hardware rendering.
*   **Coverage Map Computation:** The coverage pattern of a convex polygon for a particular tile is computed by combining the coverage maps of the polygon edges.
*   **Difference from Greene:** Do not render the visible portion of the triangle in software.
*   It is not possible to determine a priori the front-to-back relations between the triangles inside a single cell.
*   A hidden cell justifies the time invested in classification because it prevents further traversal.
